title: Book Two · Chapter 11: Two Chairs
story:
On Thursday, Miss Wu needs six chairs beside the window.

Ronan carries the first one over. He puts it close to her desk. Then he brings another.

“Leave room between them,” she says.

“There is room.”

Miss Wu sits down. The next chair touches her knee.

“Not for my legs.”

Ronan moves the second chair.

Leo comes with a third chair. He puts it much farther away.

“Long legs,” he says.

“You can sit nearer,” Miss Wu tells him. “We are reading together tomorrow. We are not calling across a field.”

Leo moves his chair back. Ronan laughs and brings the last two chairs. Jun brings the sixth.

The reading corner is not open yet. The books still stand in small piles. Some need covers. Others need names on their cards. Miss Wu puts those jobs aside for a few minutes.

She gives Ronan and Leo one story page each.

“Read this at home,” she says. “Tomorrow, our small group can read it together.”

Ronan looks at the first line. A girl and her brother are going to a shop. The girl has a basket.

He reads the next line. Then the next. Leo is still looking at the picture.

“I'm on the fourth line,” Ronan says.

“I'm looking at the door.”

“It is just a door.”

“It opens the wrong way in this picture.”

Ronan looks again. The shop door covers part of the steps. There is almost no room for the girl.

“Perhaps she climbs over it.”

Leo puts two fingers on the page. He makes the fingers jump. Jun leans over and laughs.

Miss Wu gently lifts the page from the desk.

“Please keep it flat. I need these copies tomorrow.”

She gives it back. Ronan puts it inside his book. He wants his page to stay neat. He also wants to reach the last line before Leo.

At home, Mum is marking a new sleeve length. A customer's jacket lies across her lap.

“Can I read to you?” Ronan asks.

“Yes. Let me finish this mark.”

He waits beside her chair. He moves the story away from the chalk on her fingers.

Mum puts the jacket down. Ronan begins. He goes quickly through the first few lines. The girl goes into the shop. Her brother waits at the door. The girl buys flowers.

Mum lifts one hand.

“I missed the start. Who has the basket?”

“The girl.”

“Please start there again.”

Ronan reads the first line more slowly. Mum nods. Then a customer knocks at the gate.

“I need to see her,” Mum says. “We can stop here.”

“I can finish it. There isn't much left.”

“I know. But she came for her jacket.”

Mum takes the jacket to the door. Ronan stays at the table. He reads the last lines silently. Then he folds his cloth around the page and puts it in his school bag.

At dinner, Ronan tells Dad about the six chairs. He explains the small group.

“Are you bringing my long legs?” Dad asks.

“No. Just my page.”

Dad stretches one leg under the table. Ronan pulls his foot back. Mum gives Dad a look and passes Ronan the rice.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

group＝小组；basket＝篮子；page＝书页；chair＝椅子。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan为什么需要移动第二把椅子？
2. 小故事开头是谁拿着篮子？

## 读句子

**Ronan / moves / the second chair.** Ronan／移动／第二把椅子。
